register.title: Evan Daniel's n271 certificate at 757b40b, issue664
register.headline: A smaller packing of 271 squares from Evan Daniel's basin explorer, from Couzo's packing
register.source_checks: The author reports that his two exact rational checkers, verify_cert.py (separating axes) and verify_cert2.py (polygon intersection), accept the certificate and its regularized display view. The side is the 80-digit KKT point of s271_ex1.exact.txt made rigorous by the source's exactsolve.py; the source reports a local minimum strict modulo 54 exact flat motions, no corner-corner MILP descent, 259 corner-corner contacts and 4 rattlers, and measures it against #561's packing: its load-bearing tilt angles match #561's group for group within 0.12 degrees except one group of four squares that is three here, and 2 load-bearing squares move by more than 1e-2. Those are numerical evidence, as the source says, not proofs.
register.credit: Credit Evan Daniel (https://github.com/evand/square-packing), whose basin explorer found the packing, and credit Francisco Couzo's packing of issue 561 (T-161) and Nate Chaoweeraprasit's (itsnaka, SQUISH) packing of issue 500 (T-151) that it refines as its origin, as the author asks: started from the register's witness at 271, one move of the explorer swapped the tilt angles of two neighbouring squares and a re-polish reached a different local minimum. The issue and the pinned commit state that the work was done with Claude (Claude Code) and approved by Evan Daniel.
register.next_rung: Independently review the retained replay, then adopt at 271: the certificate is below the case's ceiling (T-186) by 4.46e-5 and below every report at 271. Final exact-head CI remains required.

bibliography.note: One complete exact certificate at 757b40bc6c5f681033ff1572177d408afbf26dfe, s(271) <= 16948947733713657510723401112423/10^30, from the author's basin explorer started from the register's witness at 271; the author calls it a refinement of Francisco Couzo's #561 packing, itself refining Nate Chaoweeraprasit's #500, and a different local minimum from it, and asks that both be credited. A regularized display view of the same packing at the same side, and the source's comparison with #561's packing, are retained beside it, with the source's two exact checkers. MIT-licensed certificates and solver reports retained; Claude assistance disclosed. KKT and jamming statements are the author's numerical evidence; no local or global optimality claim.
